name: taxonomy
method: Every edge that isn't imports, calls, renders, or handles (those come from TypeScript's own resolution) read at its sites in `git show <sha>:<file>`: an http edge's URL, method, and the route file's exported handler; an external_call's client traced to its package import; a reads/writes call's receiver traced to `lib/db.ts`'s PrismaClient and its model accessor; each stores edge against `prisma/schema.prisma`'s datasource. Then every `fetch(`, `db.<model>.`, and `stripe.` call in app/, lib/, and components/ (git grep) matched to an edge, so none was missed either.
notCovered: Structural edges (imports, calls, renders, handles) aren't hand-checked; they're TypeScript's resolution, tested by the fixtures and the eval.
observations: Every `fetch(`, `db.<model>.`, and `stripe.` call site in app/, lib/, and components/ is on an edge; `stripe.webhooks.constructEvent` (app/api/webhooks/stripe/route.ts:15) has none, correctly: it verifies a signature locally and sends no request.

Account, Session, and VerificationToken have a stores edge but no reads or writes: NextAuth's `PrismaAdapter(db)` (lib/auth.ts:17) uses them from inside the library, which isn't analyzed (node_modules never is). Missing, not wrong.

At the first check (29 edges) the two unresolved edges were app/api/og/route.tsx's font loads, `fetch(new URL("../../../assets/fonts/<font>.ttf", import.meta.url))` (lines 7 and 11): a read of a file bundled with the route, not a request to a service, yet shown as `DYNAMIC_URL` ("the URL starts with a value only known at runtime"), an unresolved box for a font. M9.1a4 (ADR-0251) stops collecting such reads; re-dumped at that fix, exactly those two edges are gone and the other 27 are unchanged (same IDs, confidence, and sites), so the record now holds 27, all correct.
